## Personality

Susan is a kind-hearted, gaunt, and practical elderly spinster who approaches life with a calm disposition. Despite her unsentimental and pragmatic nature—believing poetry to be mostly untruths—she harbors a passionate tenderness when mothering a baby and holds a deep respect for the clergy. Though she is fond of men, she remains particular about certain traits, such as the appearance of ears, and can be prone to worry about safety. She is skilled at knitting stockings and baking doughnuts, but she harbors a strong distaste for big black spiders.

## History

Susan Baker, an old maid who never had a beau or married despite liking men and being willing to marry, served as household help for [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) and [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) [Blythe](../character/blythe.md). After [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) gave birth to a healthy baby boy named James Matthew, Susan, alongside friends and family, visited to admire the newborn and celebrate his arrival. When a general election resulted in a [Liberal](../codex/factions.md#liberal) victory, Captain Jim brought the news to Susan and [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md). Following a temporary absence to care for her injured sister, Susan returned from the [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen) with news and commentary, and she later discussed the Blythes' upcoming move to the [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen) with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md). At [Ingleside](../codex/places.md#ingleside), Susan cared for the family's children and routinely discussed local gossip with [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Cornelia Bryant](../character/cornelia-bryant.md), including the antics of the new minister's unruly children. She defended the children when [Cornelia](../character/cornelia-bryant.md) brought news of [Faith](../character/faith.md) Meredith's pig-riding escapade and later participated in conversations regarding town events and church politics. During one evening when the Meredith children panicked over seeing a supposed ghost in a sheet, Susan investigated the scene armed with a pitchfork and uncovered the mortifying truth that it was merely Mrs. [Stimson](../character/stimson.md) searching for a lost knitting needle. Eventually, Susan, [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md), and Miss Cornelia gathered in the evening to discuss arrangements for the children ahead of an upcoming double wedding.

_Sources: [v4 CHAPTER 22 MISS CORNELIA ARRANGES MATTERS P0](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0000), [v4 CHAPTER 22 MISS CORNELIA ARRANGES MATTERS P2](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0002), [v4 CHAPTER 22 MISS CORNELIA ARRANGES MATTERS P5](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0005), [v4 CHAPTER 22 MISS CORNELIA ARRANGES MATTERS P11](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0011), [v4 CHAPTER 22 MISS CORNELIA ARRANGES MATTERS P24](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0024), [v4 CHAPTER 34 THE SHIP O’DREAMS COMES TO HARBOR P2](../source/v04-c34.md#nw-v04-c34-p0002), +69 more_

## Quotes

> “Do not tell me,” said Susan fiercely, answering the anguish in Marilla’s eyes, “that God could be so cruel as to take that darling lamb from us when we all love her so much.”
>
> — Susan — [v4 CHAPTER 19 DAWN AND DUSK P5](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0005)

> “Now for breakfast,” she said briskly. “I am of the opinion that we will all be glad of a bite and sup. You tell young Mrs. Doctor not to worry about a single thing—Susan is at the helm. You tell her just to think of her baby.”
>
> — Susan — [v4 CHAPTER 19 DAWN AND DUSK P10](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0010)

> "Oh, the poor lamb—the poor lamb! How can she bear it, Miss Cuthbert? I am afraid it will kill her. She has been that built up and happy, longing for that baby, and planning for it. Cannot anything be done nohow, Miss Cuthbert?"
>
> — Susan — [v4 CHAPTER 19 DAWN AND DUSK P18](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0018)

> “And it is such a sweet baby,” sobbed Susan. “I never saw one so white—they are mostly red or yallow. And it opened its big eyes as if it was months old. The little, little thing! Oh, the poor, young Mrs. Doctor!”
>
> — Susan — [v4 CHAPTER 19 DAWN AND DUSK P20](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0020)

> "Have a good time and do not worry about the pantry. Susan is at the helm. There is no use in keeping a dog and doing your own barking. I am going to take your breakfast up to you every morning."
>
> — Susan — [v4 CHAPTER 22 MISS CORNELIA ARRANGES MATTERS P3](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0003)

### [Owen Ford](../character/owen-ford.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/owen-ford--susan.md)

Susan is a friend of [Owen Ford](../character/owen-ford.md), whom she admires, particularly taking pleasure in his compliments regarding her cooking. Owen frequently visits Susan's household and the surrounding area, though Susan was briefly away nursing her sister during one of his visits before returning with news from the [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen).
